info.name: SignFlow Coordination API
info.description:
JWT-authenticated coordination API of the SignFlow PDF signing desktop app.

ONE DOCUMENT, ONE SIGNER: the account that uploads a document is the account that signs it. There are no invitations, no signing order and no turn to claim, so every request here acts on the caller's own document.

Workflow:
1. Run 'Auth / Login (alice)' — the test script saves accessToken + refreshToken automatically.
2. Every other request inherits the Bearer token from the collection.
3. Access tokens expire after 15 minutes — re-run login, or use 'Auth / Refresh' (also auto-saves the rotated pair).

The signing path is 'Create workflow' then 'Submit signed PDF'. 'Register my certificate' sits between them and is needed ONLY if you created the workflow without certificateSha256 — see each request's own description.

Keep {{signerUserId}} equal to the account you log in as: routes that name a user refuse anyone else.

Requires the coordination server: double-click run-server.cmd (port 8080).

request.description: Dev passwords follow <name>-pass: alice-pass, bob-pass, charlie-pass. Wrong credentials return 401. The script stores both tokens in collection variables so every other request just works.

Rotation: each use issues a NEW refresh token (auto-saved by the script). Replaying an already-used token revokes the whole session family — try it: re-send the same request twice, the second must be 401.
Revokes the presented refresh session (204). Idempotent. After logout, Refresh returns 401.
Validates the Bearer token and returns the authenticated user id. Quick way to check token health: {"userId":"alice"}.
Workflows currently waiting for THIS user's signature. Also try switching login to bob to see turn-taking in action.

form-data: field 'request' = JSON (edit in place), field 'file' = pick any .pdf via the file selector.

One document, one signer: the signer is YOU, the authenticated caller. There is nobody to name, so the body carries the document's name and, optionally, the fingerprint of the certificate that will sign it.

certificateSha256 is OPTIONAL and decides which state the workflow starts in:
- Given (64 hex chars, colons stripped): the slot is bound, revision 0 is prepared at once, and the workflow is WAITING_FOR_SIGNER — ready for 'Download current revision' and 'Submit signed PDF'.
- Omitted: the workflow is DRAFT with audit CERTIFICATE_PENDING, and there is no revision 0 yet. 'Download current revision' answers 409 CERTIFICATE_NOT_BOUND until you run 'Register my certificate'.

For pure API testing any 64-hex value passes creation validation — but signing later requires a signature from the real bound certificate (use the app's Capture button to get the real fingerprint of the mock token). The three legacy mock-token fingerprints are refused with 422 DEVELOPMENT_IDENTITY_REJECTED unless the server accepts development identities.

Only needed when the workflow was created WITHOUT certificateSha256, i.e. it is DRAFT and has no revision 0 yet. Binding prepares the document atomically, so the answer is already WAITING_FOR_SIGNER at revision 0.

Enrollment happens on the machine the token is plugged into, which is why this is a route of its own rather than part of creation.

Rules worth knowing:
- {{signerUserId}} MUST be the account you logged in as. Binding for anybody else is 403 WORKFLOW_NOT_ACCESSIBLE — nobody can enrol a certificate on someone else's behalf.
- A slot takes a certificate ONCE: a second call is 409 CERTIFICATE_ALREADY_BOUND.
- Only while DRAFT: once prepared it is 409 INVALID_WORKFLOW_STATE.
Status overview incl. current signer and short fingerprint. Requires the logged-in user to be a workflow participant.
Returns documentRevision + documentSha256 — both are REQUIRED in the signature submission. 409 if it is not your turn.
application/pdf — only served to the signer whose turn it is (409 otherwise). Save response to a file via 'Send and Download'.
Immutable revision chain: number, parent, sha256, size, author. Revisions are never overwritten — each signature adds a new file.
Every server decision: creation, submissions, validations, rejections, turn transitions.

Upload a signature produced by the DESKTOP app (incremental update of the current revision).

Server-side checks: turn, parent revision+hash, byte-prefix append-only, full signature chain, certificate binding. Idempotent by signingOperationId — resending the same UUID returns the original result instead of a second revision.
Any participant may cancel while the workflow is still active. Terminal workflows return 409.
